key_facts: This document sets out instructions for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix held from 30 October to 1 November 2026.
The document covers general race procedures including qualifying session conduct, lapping rules, pit lane operations, practice starts, and track limits.

Drivers must allow faster drivers to overtake when blue light panels are shown (when a faster car is within 1.2 seconds), and drivers exceeding a maximum time between two Safety Car Lines during qualifying or reconnaissance laps may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly.
The document specifies that waved yellow flags and SC boards will not be used; instead, messages will be sent to all teams and trackside light panels will display SC when the Safety Car is deployed.
Track limits violations at specific turns (Turn 4, Turn 11, Turn 17) may result in lap time invalidation, rejoin restrictions, or other penalties as determined by the Stewards.
plain_explanation:
This is the Race Director's Competition Notes for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It sets out how the race will be run at this specific event, on top of the standard rules.

During qualifying and the reconnaissance laps before the race, drivers must not drive too slowly. The Race Director will give teams a maximum time between two points on the track (the Second and First Safety Car Lines). Any driver who exceeds this time on any lap during or after qualifying, or on reconnaissance laps, may be found to be driving unnecessarily slowly. This rule applies to in-laps and out-laps as well as normal laps, and also to the pit lane.

During the race, when a faster driver is catching up to a slower car ahead of them, the marshalling system will first give a warning when the gap is 3 seconds. When the gap closes to 1.2 seconds, blue light panels will be shown to the slower car (along with blue cockpit lights and a message on the timing monitors). The slower driver must then let the faster driver past at the first available opportunity. This rule comes from the International Sporting Code, which requires drivers who are caught and lapped to allow faster drivers through.

The document sets out detailed rules for pit lane operations, practice starts, and parc fermé (the sealed area where cars are kept under official supervision after qualifying and after the race). It explains where cars may and must go during these procedures, and how team personnel may enter restricted areas.

The document also specifies track limits rules for this circuit. At Turn 17, if a driver fails to take the racing line, lap times may be invalidated. At Turn 4, if a driver enters the run-off area and crosses a yellow line with all four wheels, they must rejoin the circuit at a specific point after Turn 5. At Turn 11, if a car goes completely behind the red and white kerb, there are specific rejoin rules using polystyrene blocks.

For Safety Car procedures, this event will not use waved yellow flags or SC boards. Instead, when the Safety Car is deployed, a message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent to all teams and all trackside light panels will show SC. When the Safety Car lights are turned off, a message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" will be sent, and a green light panel will appear at the Control Line.

Finally, the document lists changes made to the circuit for this race, including a resurfaced section, widened white lines at certain corners, and new positions for the practice start boxes.
